exit 0
--- stdout
Restore a BLOCKED task after the orchestrator has verified that the blocker is gone.
This is for repair completion, not normal task claiming. By default the restore
is a continuation: the task returns to the initial status for its role_pair, and
the next claim by any doer resumes its preserved work without consuming an
iteration. Pending dependencies keep that task dependency-held and
not immediately claimable. With --new-iteration, the resume consumes an
iteration. With --assign-to,
it directly restores the executing status and assigns the requested doer agent.
With --rebase-on, it rebases a preserved task worktree before unblocking, updates
base_commit, and leaves rebase conflicts BLOCKED with fresh repair metadata.
With --scope-exception-file, a coding task also receives a bounded in-task
scope exception: one strict JSON object {"files": [...], "change": "...",
"unchanged": "..."} of 1-8 repository-relative files and at most 4096 bytes.
Outside its original scope the task may then change only those files, only as
stated; acceptance, provider dependencies, review boundary and lifecycle gates
stay unchanged. Use it when the blocked task can close the gap itself in test
support, fixtures or its own constants, with production code and merged
contracts unchanged and no other unmerged writer of those files.
With --budget-exception <seconds> and --budget-ruling <decision-id>, a coding
task's canonical admission batch budget becomes the larger of its reviewed
timeout_seconds and the largest recorded exception (at most 14400). Commands,
order, manifest, proofs and deferrals stay as reviewed. Use it when admission
timed out and a human ruling authorizes the larger budget; the ruling is
recorded as given, not looked up.
Without an agent identity (no LIZA_AGENT_ID, no --agent-id) it runs as the
operator: no registration generation is needed, no role permission applies,
and --changed-by (default "human") is the audit actor.
Usage:
liza unblock-task <task-id> [flags]
Flags:
--agent-id string orchestrator agent ID (overrides LIZA_AGENT_ID; without either, runs as operator)
--allow-dirty allow tracked worktree changes during --rebase-on by using git rebase --autostash
--assign-to string doer agent ID to resume the task directly; omitted restores initial status and may remain dependency-held
--budget-exception int raise a coding task's canonical admission budget to this many seconds (requires --budget-ruling)
--budget-ruling string human decision that authorizes --budget-exception
--changed-by string identifier for audit trail (overrides LIZA_AGENT_ID env var, defaults to 'human')
--expected-transition string current task transition_id captured before the request; requires --request-id
-h, --help help for unblock-task
--json output result as structured JSON
--new-iteration make the resume consume an iteration; omitted, the next claim continues the current iteration
--reason string reason the blocked task can resume (required)
--rebase-on string branch or commit to rebase the task worktree onto before unblocking
--request-id string logical request ID; preserve with its original --expected-transition across retries
--scope-exception-file string JSON file granting a coding task a bounded in-task scope exception (files, change, unchanged)
Global Flags:
--check-update check for a Liza update before running
-C, --project-root string Liza project root for state commands
--update-channel string update check channel: stable or main (default "stable")
-v, --verbose verbose output
--- stderr
